analysis:
Reviewed the two head_text excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 44870-46475). They contain only golden test-vector data: repeated token IDs, synthetic "cache" prompt text, fixed chain hashes, a fixed prompt_contract_id and a fixed date (2028-02-29). They hold no secrets, keys, credentials or real consumer content, and no executable code. The file_changes patch shows the PR regenerates vectors: it adds `additional_context: {enable_thinking: false}` to the template_input, changes prompt_token_count and block boundary chain hashes, and shifts token_ids at about lines 3020-3926, 44524-44630 and 45471-45473. The line 45471-45473 tail change (248046, 198, 248045, 74455, 198, 248068, 271, 248069, 271) looks like a chat-template generation-prompt suffix with thinking disabled. The visible excerpts are consistent: long_prompt has prompt_token_count 1025 and four 256-token block boundaries. The visible tokens do not show the earlier segment that was truncated.

Security relevance is indirect. Prompt-contract IDs and chain hashes feed the prefix-cache keying (T-041, TB-007), so a mismatch between these fixtures and the provider or coordinator implementation could cause cross-version cache-key divergence or collisions. The supplied evidence cannot show that, because the producing Swift and Go code is not in this batch. Fixtures are test data and do not change runtime trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-011) or attestation, authorization, encryption or billing behavior. A reviewer should confirm that the generator and consumers (Swift provider and coordinator) agree on the new template, including enable_thinking handling, and that the prompt_contract_id for the new rendering stays distinct from the old rendering so that old cached prefixes are not reused. The prompt_contract_id visible at line 45511 is the only one in the supplied excerpts, so I cannot judge that. No finding is supported by the evidence supplied.
